title: Progressive Jog and Movement Series
objective: Progressively raise body temperature and prepare players for football movement patterns through progressive jog and movement series.
time: Minimum: 6 minutes | Recommended: 8 minutes | Maximum: 10 minutes
setup:
Mark a compact movement area with 4-8 cones and create clear travel lanes.
Split players into groups that allow continuous movement without queuing.
Begin at low intensity and leave enough space for safe changes of direction.
howTheDrillWorks:
Start with easy movement and gradually introduce shuffles, skips, backpedals and controlled direction changes.
Increase range of motion before increasing speed.
Finish with 2-4 sharper efforts that prepare players for the next training activity.
Use the key movement or football pattern of progressive jog and movement series as the main progression rather than adding unrelated exercises.
coachingPoints: Build intensity progressively rather than starting fast.
Keep players tall and balanced through changes of direction.
Use active arms and efficient foot placement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Players should become progressively warmer without visible fatigue.
Movement should become sharper as the drill progresses.

title: Hip Mobility Flow
objective: Improve mobility, joint range and muscular activation before higher-speed football activity using hip mobility flow.
time: Minimum: 6 minutes | Recommended: 8 minutes | Maximum: 10 minutes
setup:
Create small stations or a loose semicircle so every player can see the coach.
Allow approximately one arm span between players.
Use cones only to organise space; the emphasis is controlled quality movement.
howTheDrillWorks:
Move through the mobility pattern slowly enough to maintain posture and control.
Progress from general range-of-motion work into more dynamic football-specific positions.
Finish with active movement rather than prolonged static stretching.
Use the key movement or football pattern of hip mobility flow as the main progression rather than adding unrelated exercises.
coachingPoints: Control range; do not force mobility.
Maintain neutral posture and stable trunk position.
Move smoothly from mobility into active running.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Range of motion should improve without compensation or discomfort.
Players should remain controlled rather than rushing repetitions.

time: Minimum: 18 minutes | Recommended: 20 minutes | Maximum: 22 minutes
setup:
Adjust the area and group sizes to suit the stated warm-up purpose.
Prepare footballs, cones and bibs before players enter the activity.
Plan a clear intensity progression so the final actions match the demands of the upcoming session or match.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin at an intensity appropriate to the conditions and player group.
Progress through mobility, movement and football actions without unnecessary stoppages.
Finish at the exact intensity needed for the opening drill or match phase.
Use the key movement or football pattern of complete afl training warm-up as the main progression rather than adding unrelated exercises.
coachingPoints: Match intensity to weather, age and upcoming workload.
Progress rather than jump between intensity levels.
Finish ready for football, not fatigued by the warm-up.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Players should finish physically warm, mentally engaged and ready for the next demand.
Adjust immediately if conditions are causing players to fatigue too early.
